events.titleEn: Construction begins on the ceremonial complex at Chiripá
events.summaryEn: On the Bolivian side of Lake Titicaca, builders begin the ceremonial complex at Chiripá. One-room rectangular buildings, some with painted walls and interior niches, surround a central patio with a sunken court.
events.selectionNote: An early ceremonial centre of the Titicaca basin.

events.titleEn: An important individual is buried with a gold crown at Kuntur Wasi
events.summaryEn: An important individual is buried at Kuntur Wasi in a shaft tomb with a crown of hammered sheet gold about seven inches high, hung with fourteen human-head dangles. Ceramics from the site resemble contemporary Cupisnique wares of the north coast.
events.selectionNote: A lavish shaft-tomb burial with a gold crown.

date.noteEn: The Met dates the colonisation to about 600 BCE and gives no founding year for any single city.

events.titleEn: Milesian Greeks colonise the northern Black Sea coast
events.summaryEn: Greeks from Miletos on the Ionian coast colonise the northern Black Sea coast. They found long-lived, cosmopolitan cities such as Panticapaeum, Olbia and Pontic Chersonesus.
events.selectionNote: Greek settlement reaches the northern Black Sea coast with long-lived cities.

events.titleEn: Scythian artists develop the Animal Style
events.summaryEn: The Animal Style develops in Scythian art. The Scythians, who migrate from the Altai Mountains to the Black Sea region, depict the leopards, deer and eagles of their homeland as animals leaping, running and blending into each other; some of the best-known works are gold hammered over a carved matrix.
events.selectionNote: Dates the start of the Scythian Animal Style.

events.titleEn: San José Mogote carves the earliest recorded Zapotec date
events.summaryEn: Major buildings at San José Mogote are now built of masonry. A carved relief set in a corridor floor shows a slain figure with the hieroglyph for "1 Earthquake" between its feet, the earliest recorded date in Zapotec writing.
events.geographyEn: San José Mogote, Valley of Oaxaca, Mexico
events.selectionNote: The catalog dates the founding of Monte Albán to 500 BCE. This record covers the earlier Zapotec centre and the first dated Zapotec glyph.

date.noteEn: The Met gives Cyrus's reign as about 559–530 BCE and does not date each conquest; the range spans the reign.

events.titleEn: Cyrus the Great founds the Achaemenid empire
events.summaryEn: The Persian king Cyrus II, the Great, lays the foundation of the Achaemenid empire by overthrowing Media, Lydia and the Babylonian empire in turn.
events.selectionNote: The founding of the Achaemenid empire, which the same entry says later stretched from Greece and Egypt to Central Asia and India.

events.titleEn: Carthage and the Etruscans fight the Battle of Aleria
events.summaryEn: Carthaginian and Etruscan forces combine at the Battle of Aleria on Corsica to gain control of the Mediterranean. Soon afterwards the kingdom of Tartessos collapses.
events.selectionNote: A contest for control of the western Mediterranean; the source names the Carthaginian and Etruscan side only.
